metadata.title: The Script, Not The Understanding.
metadata.subtitle: The Workshop Skill (Coaching Script vs. Actual Understanding)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude's workshop-coaching skill guarantee the participant actually understands Claude Managed Agents by the end, or only that Claude explains things correctly along the way? Lands the carry-out that a SKILL.md file fixes exactly what Claude says, not whether it lands.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude's workshop skill would build their SEC agents for them. It doesn't do the work — it coaches you while you do it, one act at a time. Liam. Take you through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does Claude's skill do the SEC-agent workshop for me?', hesitates on 'do', corrects to 'coach', lands the real question

TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('do' -> 'coach') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is workshop — a coach for a seven-act SEC-agents training, acts zero through six. The file spells out two modes: you drive while Claude hints, or Claude makes the change and walks you through it after. Either way, it's still one text file, followed act by act.

production_viz.label: A SKILL IS A FOLDER
production_viz.caption: One file. Two modes. Same coach.

beats.narration_text: Here's the interesting constraint: even when a step breaks, Claude isn't allowed to shortcut it. The file explicitly bars reading the solutions folder or the project's git history for the fix. Instead, it checks the real documentation and the error message, fixes it forward, and explains what changed — the same explanation it gives when the step just works. Stuck or not, the explanation has to come from understanding the stub, never from copying a known answer.

shot.new_visual_element: NO PEEKING AT THE ANSWER KEY

production_viz.label: NO PEEKING AT THE ANSWER KEY
production_viz.caption: Stuck or not: reason it, don't copy it.

beats.narration_text: The file also fixes exactly how each explanation is shaped: what changed, why it works, the platform idea behind it, where to see it live, one thing to try. That's the artifact — Claude's coaching script. Whether the participant actually walks away understanding how a managed agent works is a different thing entirely, and no text file can promise that part.

production_viz.label: THE SCRIPT, AND THE LEARNING
production_viz.caption: The file reaches the middle step. Not the last one.

beats.narration_text: A SKILL.md file can fix exactly what Claude says next. It can't fix whether the person listening actually understands it.

props.quote: A SKILL.md file can fix exactly what Claude says next. It can't fix whether the person listening actually understands it.
props.sparkLine: Fixes the script. Not the grasp.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Write a short, five-part coaching file — what changed, why it works, the concept it shows, where to see it, one thing to try — for walking someone through fixing an off-by-one bug in a for loop. Follow those exact steps to coach me through one I'll paste in. Then ask me to explain the fix back in my own words, and tell me honestly whether that proves I understood it, or just that I could repeat you.
